findings.current: Thanked me for saving their tribespeople and families.
findings.defect: “Families” loses the source’s specific reference to blood relatives.
findings.rationale: The Korean explicitly says 부족민들과 혈육, distinguishing the tribespeople from their blood kin.
findings.replacement: They thanked me for saving their tribespeople and blood relatives.

findings.current: You were gone so long that I had a feeling something had happened…
findings.defect: This changes the specific cue from waiting for him without his arrival to him being gone a long time.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly says they waited, he still did not come, and she could infer what happened; the current line omits the waiting and non-arrival.
findings.replacement: When you didn’t come even after we waited, I had a pretty good idea what must have happened…
findings.source: Line 13: “기다려도 안 오시길래 충분히 짐작은 했는데……”

findings.current: “Of course it’s a first. An outsider attending the tribal grand council was a first, and that outsider getting into a fight with the great chieftain of the Bai people was a first too. Yes, indeed.”
findings.defect: The narration omits Namho’s warm smile and that he was beside Ju Hwaran when he added his comment.
findings.rationale: The source includes both Namho’s position beside Ju Hwaran and his warm smile as part of the moment.
findings.replacement: At Ju Hwaran’s astonished expression, Namho, who was beside her, added with a warm smile, “Of course it’s a first. An outsider attending the tribal grand council was a first, and that outsider getting into a fight with the great chieftain of the Bai people was a first too. Yes, indeed.”
findings.source: Line 15: “놀라는 주화란의 모습에, 옆에 있던 남호가 푸근한 미소를 지으며 덧붙였다.”

summary: The translation is largely faithful, but it loses the blood-kin detail in one line and omits an explicit waiting detail and a character beat.
